_comment: Golden vectors for the store-and-forward (courier) wire format.
Byte-compatible with bitchat-ios CourierEnvelope. Published so a second
implementation can be written without reading the TypeScript, and asserted
by src/core/mesh/courier/__tests__/courier-vectors.test.ts against the running code,
so this file cannot go stale while the suite is green.
The format earns vectors because three ways of getting it wrong fail
SILENTLY: the envelope is accepted, carried, then dropped at deposit with
nothing logged at either end.
1. expiry is MILLISECONDS. Seconds is ~1000x too small, so every envelope
reads as long expired.
2. the copies TLV is OMITTED at 1, not written as 1. A decoder that
requires it rejects every carry-only envelope.
3. the recipient tag is keyed on the recipient's PUBLIC Noise key and
rotates daily. Wrong epoch-day arithmetic produces a tag no carrier
matches, so mail is never delivered.
bitchat's own set is kept separately, as published, in
courier-test-vectors-bitchat.json, and the same test checks the code
against both.
HMAC-SHA256(key = recipient's 32-byte public Noise static key,
msg = 'bitchat-courier-tag-v1' || epochDay as u32 BE)[0:16].
epochDay = floor(unixMillis / 86400000).
NOT unlinkable, inherited rather than chosen. The HMAC key is the
recipient's PUBLIC key, which every announce broadcasts, so anyone who has
heard one announce can compute that peer's tags for any day and follow
their mail. bitchat documents the same flaw. Changing it unilaterally
breaks courier interop for no gain: every carrier on both sides would have
to change together.
recipientTag.label: bitchat-courier-tag-v1

_comment: Type-length-value, u16 big-endian lengths, in this exact order:
0x01 recipientTag  16 bytes
0x02 expiry         8 bytes, u64 BE, UNIX MILLISECONDS
0x03 ciphertext     variable, the Noise X output
0x04 copies         1 byte, OMITTED entirely when copies == 1
0x05 prekeyID       optional; present only on forward-secret v2
envelopes, where the ciphertext is sealed to a
one-time prekey rather than the static key. A v1
decoder skips it as an unknown type and still
carries the envelope opaquely.

cases._comment: Sprayable: copies > 1, so the 0x04 TLV is present.

_comment: Carry-only: copies == 1, so the 0x04 TLV is absent rather than
written as 1. This is the case a fresh implementation gets wrong, and
the resulting rejection is invisible on both sides.
A carrier judges an envelope by its own limits, not the sender's. An
expiry beyond ttl + slack is refused outright rather than clamped, so a
sender that stamps longer does not get longer carriage, it gets none.
